report:
Reviewed the complete provider_authority claim, its sole ordinary implementation association (sage_ir::tcx, tcx/mod.rs), and its complete associated test set (sage_meta::todo::metadata_provider_authority). Independently verified exact byte equality of both current implementation and test files against the historical snapshot. Claim and implementation metadata are unchanged; historical test source now lives in the test fragment rather than metadata, with the same test identity/status and body. Prior rationale is consistent with current evidence, not a substitute for this assessment.

Source assessment: TcxDb returns owned strings, IDs, vectors and Raw* records for external definitions, paths, signatures, predicates, impl headers, associated values and candidate inventories. Its API has no Sage-local syntax resolver, chosen Sage candidate result, Sage proof result, alias normalization operation, or checked Sage body product. relevant_trait_impls returns a candidate inventory with completeness, and inherent_method_candidates returns identities/visibility, not a selected method. associated_type_value returns an external declaration value, not normalization of a Sage goal. adt_is_always_sized supplies a universal external nominal fact rather than deciding a particular Sage instantiation; the documented false case explicitly is not such a proof. Proc-macro methods return expanded text and do not resolve or type-check that text. These distinctions match the captured architectural-foundations section: external compiler/dependency facts may be authoritative while local semantic decisions remain in Sage.

The sole test is explicitly TODO and has no assertions. It therefore establishes none of these prohibitions behaviorally. Its comment retains the missing interface verification matrix and end-to-end evidence that Sage candidate and solver queries execute after metadata receipt. This is a justified visible verification deferral: completion requires interface boundary checks and instrumented end-to-end scenarios for local resolution, candidate selection, goal proof, alias normalization and checked bodies using external raw facts. Current interface inspection supports the intended separation but does not establish all provider implementations or downstream execution paths. No deferred behavior is relabeled implemented; no additional edit is needed to the existing accounting.

Execution: personally ran review start with the assigned instruction file, review read for review policy and the relevant architectural rationale, byte comparison, and review record. No behavior tests or workspace build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator-reported 321-test suite and cargo build are separate baseline evidence, not proof of this TODO contract.
